evals.prompt: I want to add a rate limiting section to docs/architecture/api.md. My draft is at `.claude/skills/docs-writing/evals/files/rate-limiting-draft.md.txt` (line numbers refer to that file). Review it and give me a fixed version.
evals.expected_output: Findings first, one per line as '<line>  <category>  <finding and suggested text>' under the draft's path, ordered facts, then structure, then style, ending with a count per category; then the fixed section. Facts checked against the code: @fastify/rate-limit is registered with global: false in apps/api/src/plugins/security.ts and only sign-up, sign-in and password change opt in (config.rateLimit in apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts); the default AUTH_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE is 10 (apps/api/src/config.ts), not 100; the count is per client IP (request.ip, TRUST_PROXY), not per account; the page already covers the limit in Access layers and Configuration. The fixed version removes the 'As of September 2026' date, tags the code block and drops the '$' prompt, uses sentence case without a colon subtitle, cuts filler, the em dash and the exclamation mark, and gives the link descriptive text. Skill-only: #1, #2, #3 (SKILL.md › Reviewing instead of writing, references/checklist.md › Review output format), #5 (SKILL.md › House rules: no dates like 'as of'), #6 ('$' prompt rule in references/style.md › Code blocks).
assertions: Before the fixed version, findings are listed one per line, each with a line number from the draft file and a category label (fact, structure, style or equivalent)
Every fact finding is listed before any style finding (findings ordered by impact rather than by line number or by word)
The findings end with a total count broken down by category (for example '9 findings: 3 fact, 2 structure, 4 style')

Fact findings correct all three wrong claims, matching the code: the limit applies only to sign-up, sign-in and password change (global: false in apps/api/src/plugins/security.ts, config.rateLimit in apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts), the default AUTH_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE is 10 rather than 100, and requests are counted per client IP rather than per user account
The fixed version removes the 'As of September 2026' date instead of keeping or updating it
The fixed version's code block has a language tag and the command has no leading '$ ' prompt
